resources.string: Why is the overlay hidden?
Every reason the readout can disappear
An app will not accept my taps
How to pause the overlay for a moment
Rules you can turn off
Screen off
Sampling stops with the screen and resumes when it turns on.
Lock screen
Android never shows app overlays on the lock screen.
Offline
When the chosen counters have nothing to read, the readout hides or shows dashes, per Behavior.
Idle
Hide when idle is on and traffic stayed under the threshold.
Fullscreen app
Hide in fullscreen is on and an app hid the status bar.
Landscape
Hide in landscape is on and the phone is turned sideways.
Battery Saver
Pause on Battery Saver is on and Battery Saver is active.
Android hides it for you
System settings and dialogs
Every Settings page, permission prompt, and installer hides all app overlays while it is open.
Secure screens
Payment, banking, and password screens can block overlays; Android gives no signal.
The app is off or paused
Paused
A pause from Home, the tile, the notification, or a shortcut hides it until it ends.
Permission removed
Turning off Display over other apps stops the overlay; Home shows how to restore it.
An app will not accept my taps
What is happening
Android blocks touches under overlays
Some apps refuse taps while any overlay is on screen, to stop tapjacking.
Pixel Speed cannot bypass it
The only fix is to hide the overlay for a moment.
Opacity past the limit
An overlay more opaque than Android allows blocks the taps under it. Lower Opacity under Appearance.
Ways to pause
Home
The pause card offers your durations or until you resume.
Quick Settings tile
Add the Pixel Speed tile; a tap pauses or resumes, and with several profiles it opens the picker.
Notification
The status notification carries a pause action.
Launcher shortcut
Long-press the app icon for Pause and Toggle shortcuts.
Automation apps
Turn on Advanced mode under System, switch on Automation broadcasts, then broadcast pause or resume.
A system notice keeps coming back
How to silence the notice about drawing over other apps
Android posts it, not Pixel Speed
The lock screen hides every app overlay. After an unlock, Android treats the overlay\'s return as a new one, so the notice that Pixel Speed is displaying over other apps comes back each time.
Swiping it away does not last
The next unlock brings it back. Turning its category off does last, and only affects this notice.
Silence it for good
1. Long-press the notice
Pull down the shade and hold the notice until its options open.
2. In those options, tap Turn off
Not the Turn off button on the notice itself: that one removes the overlay permission and stops Pixel Speed.
3. Switch off Pixel Speed\'s row and tap Apply
The row reads “Pixel Speed displaying over other apps”. The notice does not come back.
Report a problem
What to send, and a diagnostics file to attach
What helps
Say what happened and what you expected
Steps that bring it back help most. Say whether it happens every time or now and then.
Add a picture
A screenshot of the status bar settles most placement reports. A short screen recording settles a flicker.
The diagnostics file
What it holds

The app version, the phone model and Android version, the display and cutout geometry, which permissions are granted, the readout\'s state, your settings export with your profile names, the app\'s own recent log lines, and the last crash if one was caught.
What it never holds
No account, no device id, no serial number, no location, nothing from other apps. Nothing is sent on its own: you open the file, then share it where you want.
